original_question: Let V_{d1,...,dk} be the Segre-Veronese variety of partially symmetric rank-one tensors in P(S^{d1}V1 ⊗ ··· ⊗ S^{dk}Vk). For each r, the r-th secant variety σ_r(V_{d1,...,dk}) has expected dimension min{r dim(V_{d1,...,dk}) + r - 1, ambient dimension}. Which Segre-Veronese varieties are r-defective (that is, have secant variety of smaller than expected dimension), and what are the actual dimensions of their secant varieties?
target_in_paper: Problem 1 in Section 1.1 ("Dimension of secant varieties"), with the immediately stated Terracini-lemma reformulation as Problem 2.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right family of varieties (Segre-Veronese varieties of partially symmetric rank-one tensors), the correct secant-variety setup, the expected-dimension count, the definition of r-defectivity, and the goal of determining the actual secant dimensions in the defective cases. This is essentially the content of Problem 1 in the paper, expanded into a more explicit stand-alone form.
missing_details: The paper works over the complex numbers by default; this global convention is stated in the Notation section.

The Segre-Veronese variety is defined as the image of the embedding v_{d_1,...,d_k}: P V_1 × ··· × P V_k → P(S^{d_1}V_1 ⊗ ··· ⊗ S^{d_k}V_k), where V_i are finite-dimensional complex vector spaces of dimensions n_i.
The multidegrees d_1,...,d_k are assumed to be non-negative integers.
The problem is quantified over all integers r ≥ 1 and, implicitly, over all tuples of dimensions and multidegrees; this should be stated explicitly if the question is to be fully stand-alone.
The expected dimension in the paper is written as min{r dim X + r - 1, dim(ambient vector space) - 1}; in your draft, 'ambient dimension' should be clarified to mean the ambient projective dimension.
The dimension of the Segre-Veronese variety itself is implicit in your draft; for X = v_{d_1,...,d_k}(P V_1 × ··· × P V_k), one has dim X = Σ_i (n_i - 1).

If one wants the exact paper-faithful reformulation, the paper immediately translates the defectivity problem into the equivalent question of when the corresponding multidegree line bundle on P V_1 × ··· × P V_k is special, i.e. when r generic double points fail to impose independent conditions.
The paper phrases this as an open classification problem, not as a request restricted to currently known defective cases only.
No additional homogeneity, operator, or nilpotency hypotheses occur here beyond the multidegree data d_1,...,d_k.
refined_question: Over C, let V_1,...,V_k be finite-dimensional vector spaces of dimensions n_1,...,n_k, and let d_1,...,d_k be non-negative integers. Let X = V_{d_1,...,d_k} be the image of the Segre-Veronese embedding v_{d_1,...,d_k}: P V_1 × ··· × P V_k → P(S^{d_1}V_1 ⊗ ··· ⊗ S^{d_k}V_k). For each integer r ≥ 1, classify all tuples (n_1,...,n_k; d_1,...,d_k; r) for which the secant variety σ_r(X) is defective, i.e. dim σ_r(X) < min{r dim X + r - 1, dim(S^{d_1}V_1 ⊗ ··· ⊗ S^{d_k}V_k) - 1}, and determine dim σ_r(X) in every defective case.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for X = P V_1 × ··· × P V_k and the multidegree line bundle O_X(d_1,...,d_k), classify for which integers r ≥ 1 the bundle O_X(d_1,...,d_k) is special in the sense that r generic double points on X fail to impose independent conditions on H^0(O_X(d_1,...,d_k)); by Terracini's Lemma, this is equivalent to the r-defectivity of the corresponding Segre-Veronese variety.
justification: The draft is targeting the opening problem of Section 1.1, not a broader neighboring topic. The paragraph immediately before Problem 1 introduces the expected-dimension bound and the definition of r-defectivity, and Problem 1 itself is exactly 'Classify defective Segre-Veronese varieties and determine their dimension.' The next paragraph then gives the paper's only explicit equivalent reformulation relevant here: via Terracini's Lemma, the defectivity question is rephrased as the speciality of the corresponding line bundles on products of projective spaces. So the sharp paper-faithful refinement is to keep the question as a global classification of defective Segre-Veronese secant varieties, while making the ambient field, embedding, quantifiers, and dimension formula fully explicit.
